auth.title: Use OAuth 2.0 to Access Google Ads API  |  Google for Developers
highlights:
Note: In addition to the OAuth 2.0 credentials, you also need a developer token to make API calls.

Just like other Google APIs, Google Ads API also uses the OAuth 2.0 protocol for authentication and authorization. OAuth 2.0 enables your Google Ads API client app to access a user's Google Ads account without having to handle or store the user's login info.

Broadly speaking, all the OAuth 2.0 authorization scenarios that Google supports also works with Google Ads API. However, we will focus on a handful of scenarios that are most common for Google Ads API developers.

| Scenario | Recommended approach |
| --- | --- |
| My app already uses one or more Google APIs. I have already built support for OAuth 2.0 workflows for my app, and just need to add Google Ads API functionality to my existing app. |   Make sure your authorized user or your service account has access to the Google Ads API accounts you are making API calls to. Learn more about the Google Ads access model. Refer to the  multi-user authentication workflow or the  service account workflow depending on the approach you are using with the rest of the Google APIs that your app is using.   |
| I am building an app that manages Google Ads accounts that I already have access to. If I need to manage new Google Ads accounts in the future, I will gain access to those accounts by linking them under my Google Ads Manager account.  OR  Someone will invite me to manage those accounts.  |  Use service account workflow. If you have organizational policies that prevent you from using service accounts, then use  single-user authentication workflow as a fallback.  |
| I am building an app that manages Google Ads accounts on behalf of other users. My app will build a user screen that lets the logged in users to connect to their Google Ads accounts and authorize my app to manage those accounts on their behalf. | Use multi-user authentication. |

To review and revoke access for third-party applications connected to your Google Account, visit your Google Account permissions page.

highlights:
You need both OAuth 2.0 application credentials and a developer token when calling the Google Ads API. If you're making API calls with a Google Ads manager account, you also need to specify a`login-customer-id` header with each request. This page describes how to set these values and documents several additional API-specific HTTP headers that are sent and received when using the REST interface.

## OAuth 2.0 credentials

The Google Ads API uses application credentials for identifying and authorizing API requests. Both OAuth 2.0 clients and service accounts can be configured. For more details about configuring client-side authorization, see OAuth2 in the Google Ads API.

If you are new to Google APIs, you can use oauth2l or the OAuth 2.0 Playground to experiment with application credentials and the Google Ads API before writing the code for your app.

### Using desktop or web app flows

Follow the steps to configure a Google API Console project for the Google Ads API. Record the client ID and client secret, then come back to this page.

Once you've created an OAuth client, follow the desktop app flow instructions or the web app flow instructions to generate a refresh token and an access token.

### Using service accounts

Follow the common instructions in the Service Accounts guide to set up service account access for the Google Ads API.

Once you've set up a service account to access your Google Ads account, follow the Using OAuth 2.0 for Server to Server Applications guide, making sure to select the`HTTP/REST` tab. The`scope` to use for Google Ads API access is`https://www.googleapis.com/auth/adwords`.

### Generating new access tokens

Once you have a client ID, client secret, and refresh token, you can generate a new access token for use in API calls with the curl command line tool:

```
curl \
  --data "grant_type=refresh_token" \
  --data "client_id=CLIENT_ID" \
  --data "client_secret=CLIENT_SECRET" \
  --data "refresh_token=REFRESH_TOKEN" \
  https://www.googleapis.com/oauth2/v3/token
```

You then use the access token returned by the curl request in the`Authorization` HTTP header of every API call to the Google Ads API:

```
GET /v21/customers:listAccessibleCustomers HTTP/1.1
Host: googleads.googleapis.com
Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN
developer-token: DEVELOPER_TOKEN

```

## Request headers

### Developer token

The Google Ads API also requires a developer token in order to make calls to the API. You can apply for a token for your manager account directly from the Google Ads UI. For more details about getting set up with a developer token, see Obtain Your Developer Token.

You need to include your developer token value in the`developer-token` HTTP header of every API call to the Google Ads API:

```
GET /v21/customers:listAccessibleCustomers HTTP/1.1
Host: googleads.googleapis.com
Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN
developer-token: DEVELOPER_TOKEN

```

### Login customer ID

For Google Ads API calls made by a manager to a client account (that is, when logging in as a manager to make API calls to one of its client accounts), you also need to supply the`login-customer-id` HTTP header. This value represents the Google Ads customer ID of the manager making the API call.

Including this header is equivalent to choosing an account in the Google Ads UI after signing in or clicking on your profile image at the top-right corner of the page. When specifying the customer ID, be sure to remove any hyphens (—), for example:`1234567890`, not`123-456-7890`.

```
GET /v21/customers:listAccessibleCustomers HTTP/1.1
Host: googleads.googleapis.com
Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN
developer-token: DEVELOPER_TOKEN
login-customer-id: MANAGER_CUSTOMER_ID

```

auth.title: Set up a Google API Console project  |  Google Ads API  |  Google for Developers
highlights:
The steps to be followed for creating and configuring a Google API Console project depends on the type of OAuth 2.0 authorization scenario you are building in your application. Choose the authorization scenario you are building for; this guide will be customized based on your choice.

You need a Google API Console project for creating OAuth 2.0 credentials, and enabling the Google Ads API for your app.

The credentials are needed for the authentication and authorization of Google Ads users by Google servers. These credentials let you generate OAuth tokens to be used in calls to the API.

Although you can use a single developer token for multiple projects, each project can use only a single developer token.

## Select or create a Google API Console project

Note: If you already have a Google API Console project and want to use it to create credentials, you can skip to Enable the Google Ads API in your project. However, you shouldn't have used this project for Google Ads API access in the past with another developer token.

Follow the instructions to create a project. Enabling billing for your project is optional. If you have billing enabled, select a billing account for the new project. There is no charge for using the Google Ads API, but there is a quota on the total number of Cloud projects.

## Enable the Google Ads API in your project

To enable the Google Ads API in your project, follow these steps:

1. Open the API Library in the Google API Console. If prompted, select your project or create a new one. The API Library lists all available APIs, grouped by product family and popularity.
2. Use search to find the Google Ads API if it isn't visible in the list.
3. Select the Google Ads API, then click the Enable button.

## Create a service account and key

Note: If you are already using another Google API and have created an OAuth 2.0 service account and key, you can skip this step and reuse the existing credentials.

Start by creating a service account and credentials. Next, create credentials for the service account. Download the service account key in JSON format and note the service account ID and email.

highlights:
The developer token is a 22-character long alphanumeric string that was used to connect your app to the Google Ads API. Developer tokens were sunset on September 9, 2026. This guide summarizes the changes and lists the frequently asked questions about this migration to assist the existing developers.

Key Point: New to the Google Ads API? You no longer need a developer token or a Google Ads manager account to get started. API access is now managed directly in your Google Cloud project: enabling the API grants Test access (15,000 operations per day on test accounts), and you can apply on the Google Ads API Overview page for Explorer access (automated review and approval in most cases, for up to 2,880 operations per day on production accounts). Follow the Make your first call quickstart or connect an AI assistant with the Google Ads MCP server.

...

### API access levels are associated with Google Cloud projects

We sunset developer tokens on September 9, 2026. Your current and active developer token access level was automatically transferred to your Google Cloud projects based on API activity in the 90 days preceding the sunset. You can continue sending developer tokens in your API call headers, but this is optional and ignored by the API servers. Your existing code will continue working without any changes. Your API access levels are determined by the Google Cloud project you used to generate your OAuth credentials.

- If your app uses the user authentication workflow, then this is the project that owns your OAuth client ID and secret.
- If you use the service account workflow, then this is the project that owns your service account.

auth.title: Authentication and authorization  |  Google Ads API  |  Google for Developers
highlights:
## Credentials Copy link to this section: Credentials

Access to the Google Ads API requires OAuth 2.0 credentials and, in some cases, a login customer ID.

Copy link to this section: OAuth 2.0 credentials

To authorize as Google Account users with access to Google Ads accounts, you must provide a set of OAuth 2.0 credentials. The type of credentials required varies depending on the OAuth 2.0 flow being used.

The library supports three flows:

- Service account flow
- Single-user authentication flow
- Multi-user authentication flow

Refer to the OAuth overview for details on Google Ads API OAuth flows, and follow the instructions for the flow that best meets your needs to obtain the required credentials.

### Login customer ID Copy link to this section: Login customer ID

Optionally, specify the customer ID of a manager account that provides access to the serving account. This must be specified if your access to the customer account is through a manager account. There is no need to specify all manager accounts on the path to the customer ID, only the topmost manager ID that you are using for access permissions. For more details, see the related documentation.

In the client library, the login customer ID is specified by the `api.googleads.loginCustomerId` key in your `ads.properties` file.

...

## OAuth workflows

There are three common workflows used when working with the Google Ads API.

### Service account flow

This is the recommended workflow if your workflow doesn't require any human interaction. This workflow requires a configuration step, where the user adds a service account to their Google Ads account. The app can then use the service account's credentials to manage the user's Google Ads account.

Once you have the private key JSON file, add the following to your `ads.properties` file:

```
api.googleads.serviceAccountSecretsPath=INSERT_PATH_TO_JSON_HERE
# Only add this key if you are using Google Workspace domain-wide delegation
# to impersonate a user who has access to the Google Ads account.
# api.googleads.serviceAccountUser=USER_EMAIL_TO_IMPERSONATE

```

Refer to the service account workflow guide to learn more.

### Single-user authentication flow

This workflow may be used if you cannot use service accounts. This workflow requires two configuration steps:

1. Give a single user access to all the accounts to be managed using the Google Ads API. A common approach is to grant the user access to a Google Ads API manager account and link all target Google Ads accounts under that manager account.
2. The user runs a command-line tool such as `gcloud` CLI or the `GenerateUserCredentials` code example to authorize your app to manage all their Google Ads accounts on their behalf.

Once you have these credentials, add the following to your `ads.properties` file:

api.googleads.clientId=

INSERT_CLIENT_ID_HERE

api.googleads.clientSecret=

INSERT_CLIENT_SECRET_HERE

api.googleads.refreshToken=

INSERT_REFRESH_TOKEN_HERE

Refer to the single-user authentication workflow guide to learn more.

### Multi-user authentication flow

This is the recommended workflow if your app allows users to sign in and authorize your app to manage their Google Ads accounts on their behalf. The `GenerateUserCredentials` code example is a command-line tool that illustrates how to obtain user authentication at runtime to manage their Google Ads accounts on their behalf. You can use this code example as a reference to build desktop or web apps that require user authentication.

For multi-user applications, store your application's OAuth 2.0 client ID and client secret in `ads.properties` (or another configuration store), while storing each end user's refresh token securely in your application database and passing it programmatically at runtime when building `UserCredentials` and `GoogleAdsClient`:

api.googleads.clientId=

INSERT_CLIENT_ID_HERE

api.googleads.clientSecret=

INSERT_CLIENT_SECRET_HERE

Refer to the multi-user authentication workflow guide to learn more.

auth.title: Service Account Workflow  |  Google Ads API  |  Google for Developers
highlights:
This guide discusses how to access the Google Ads API with service accounts.

A service account is an account that belongs to your app instead of to an individual end user. Service accounts employ an OAuth 2.0 flow that doesn't require human authorization, using instead a key file that only your app can access.

Using service accounts provides two key benefits:

- Authorization for Google Ads API access to Google Ads accounts is done as a configuration step, leveraging the authorization and account management features offered by the Google Ads UI. This saves developer effort by not having to build OAuth 2.0 flows and deal with complication that involve user interaction, storing user credentials, etc.
- Authorization for access to Google Ads accounts is not tied to individual user credentials, which may be useful in cases such authorization is expected to continue even if the employee who originally authorized the access leaves the team or the company.

## Account access setup

Note: You can associate up to 20 Google Ads accounts (including Google Ads manager accounts) with a single email address. If you need to manage more than 20 accounts using a service account, we recommend adding the service account to a Google Ads manager account instead, and linking all your accounts under this manager account. Refer to the access model guide to learn more.

1. Start by creating a service account and credentials.

Download the service account key in JSON format and note the service account ID and email.
2. Sign in to your Google Ads account as an administrator. Navigate to Admin > Access and security.
3. Click the + button under the Users tab.
4. Type the service account email into the Email input box. Select the appropriate level of account access level and click the Add account button.
5. The service account is granted access.
6. [Optional] By default, you cannot grant administrator access to a service account. If your API calls require administrator access, you can upgrade the access as follows.

- Click the drop-down arrow next to the access level of the service account in the Access level column.
- Select Admin from the drop-down list.

...

You can also refer to Google's OAuth documentation to learn more about the raw HTTP workflow for service accounts.

Start by setting the service account as the active credentials in gcloud CLI.

```
gcloud auth login --cred-file=PATH_TO_CREDENTIALS_JSON
```

Next, fetch an OAuth 2.0 access token for the Google Ads API.

```
gcloud auth \
  print-access-token \
  --scopes='https://www.googleapis.com/auth/adwords'
```

You can now use the access token in your API calls.

### A new signup experience for the Google Ads API

Note: If you are a developer who needs access to the App Conversion Tracking API, you should continue to sign up for a developer token from the API Center page instead.

You can sign up for access to Google Ads API directly in the Google Cloud Console without requiring a Google Ads manager account. Don't sign up for a developer token from the API Center page or attempt to apply for API access from the API Center page in your Google Ads manager account as these processes have been transitioned to Google Cloud Console and won't be processed if initiated from the API Center page.

...

We have sunset all the new signup and API access management functionality such as applying for API access and managing API access levels in the API Center page in Google Ads manager accounts. These functionalities are available in the Google Ads API Overview page in Google Cloud Console instead.

...

### Brand verification is required for Basic and Standard access

For new Basic and Standard access applications, you must complete brand verification for your Google Cloud project. Existing access holders are not required to complete brand verification, though it is encouraged.

Basic access applications are automated and will be reviewed within minutes after brand verification and submission.

Because of these process updates, all pending Basic access applications are closed as part of this transition. Affected applicants receive an email with details and should re-apply for Basic access from the Google Ads API Overview page.

...

### Users are not given Explorer access or Basic access even after completing Brand verification

We are aware of an issue where some users with brand verified projects are rejected when applying for Basic access. The users will receive a rejection email that says "Basic Access requires a successfully verified OAuth brand profile. Your application could not be approved because you haven't completed brand verification for your project." Similarly, some users signing up for Explorer access are also rejected with a rejection email that says "At this time, we are unable to grant Explorer Access to your Google Cloud project because it does not meet the eligibility criteria required for direct production account access under our Google Ads API Policies and Terms of Service."

#### Root cause

Your Google Cloud project may be on Google Cloud Free Trial program or has a suspended or disabled billing account.

#### How to verify

Check your Google Cloud billing status. If your billing project shows as "Free trial account" or is in a suspended or disabled state, you are affected by this issue.

#### Status

We have identified the root cause and are working on a fix for this issue.

#### Temporary workaround

There are several workarounds to resolve this issue. Select the most suitable option for your use case.

Upgrade your Google Cloud project to a paid tier

Upgrade your Google Cloud project to a paid tier. Wait for a few minutes and try applying for Basic access again.

Remove billing for your Google Cloud project

Warning: Removing billing will turn off all other paid Google Cloud services running in that project and may have other undesired effects. Use this workaround only if you plan to use this project exclusively for your Google Ads API integration or if you are comfortable temporarily pausing other cloud services.

If you don't have other services running in your Google Cloud project, remove billing for your Google Cloud project. Wait for a few minutes and try applying for Basic access again.

Use a different Google Cloud project

If you have another Google Cloud project that is brand verified, use that project to apply for Basic access.

...

### My developer token was part of an allowlist. How am I affected?

Google may run pilot programs that give some developers access to experimental features. The access to these features are sometimes provided by adding your developer token to an allowlist. If you were part of such a pilot program, then no action is required from your side.

We have updated all the pilot programs to use Google Cloud projects instead of developer tokens as the allowlisting mechanism and transferred the developer token's allowlist status to the associated Google Cloud projects. Your existing code should continue to work without any changes. If you continue facing issues, reach out to your Google Account manager who enrolled you into the pilot program.

gate.title: Access levels and RMF  |  Google Ads API  |  Google for Developers
highlights:
The Google Ads API has access levels associated with the Google Cloud project, and uses an application review process to grant various access levels. It's important to plan and obtain the correct access levels before productionizing your application.

A common scenario is that your application development starts with Explorer access level, but then outgrows its quota limits over time. At that point, you should apply for Basic access level or Standard access level. While Basic access applications are reviewed automatically, the Standard access review process can take several business days or sometimes weeks to complete, so request your Standard access level upgrade well before you need the increased quota limits.

Google may require that your app provide certain capabilities or features as listed in the Required Minimum Functionality (RMF). When using the Google Ads API, the RMF only applies to Google Cloud projects with Standard access level. Make sure you review these requirements in advance to avoid additional delays around building the necessary features in your app.

## Pricing Copy link to this section: Pricing

The Google Ads API is free to use; there are no charges for using the Google Ads API at Explorer access, Basic access, or Standard access levels. However, if you are subject to Required Minimum Functionality (RMF), the API Review Team audits your tool for compliance. If the audit results in a finding of non-compliance, you may be required to pay non-compliance fees.

gate.title: Test accounts  |  Google Ads API  |  Google for Developers
highlights:
Test accounts let you try out new API implementations or account configurations prior to implementing the changes in your production environment.

While production accounts serve ads that require billing and are rendered to users, test accounts appear in the Google Ads UI as cancelled accounts since there is no active billing and they don't render ads to users.

Because test and production accounts cannot interact in any way, you cannot use a test account under your existing production manager account. To use test accounts, you need a new account hierarchy, with a test manager account as the root.

...

## Why use test accounts?

Test accounts don't affect your live ads or charge your account, hence they're a useful way to experiment with the API. Test accounts provide extra benefits during active development. Particularly, test accounts:

- Can be set up in a hierarchy and organized just like production accounts.
- Can be viewed and manipulated in the Google Ads UI, just like production accounts.
- Don't require an approved developer token, so you can start experimenting with the API immediately, even before your application is reviewed or approved.
- Can't serve ads or interact with your production accounts in any way. This gives you a safe environment to test code or configuration changes without impacting your serving accounts.
- Have the same restrictions, including rate limits, as production accounts.

Since test accounts don't have budgets, you might see an error when creating a test sub-account in a manager account.

...

## Limitations

Test accounts are a great option for testing changes before deploying them to production, or developing your application while your developer token has test account access. However, there are some limitations to keep in mind.

- Because test accounts can't serve ads or interact with your production accounts in any way, serving metrics -- like impressions, conversions, or cost data -- are empty.
- Some features cannot be tested with test accounts. This includes bid simulations, conversion uploads, and billing. Other features, including recommendations, have limited capabilities within test accounts because test accounts don't generate serving data.
- Test manager account hierarchies can contain up to 50 test accounts.
- Test accounts generating a high volume of continuous requests may be throttled without notice.

mcp.title: Google Ads MCP server: Developer integration guide  |  Google Ads API  |  Google for Developers
highlights:
The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that lets large language models (LLMs) securely interact with external data and applications. The Google Ads MCP server provides a standardized bridge to the Google Ads API. It lets AI agents retrieve and analyze account data, create assets, upload videos, and manage labels by using natural language.

...

## Technical overview Copy link to this section: Technical overview

Integrating the Google Ads MCP server removes the need to write custom code for Google Ads API authentication, resource fetching, data parsing, and supported asset or label mutations. The server exposes callable tools and reference resources (see Core capabilities) that an LLM can inspect and invoke.

### Key specifications Copy link to this section: Key specifications

- Protocol: MCP (Model Context Protocol)
- Mode: Read and partial mutate (asset creation, video uploads, and label management with propose-and-confirm validation, or configurable read-only mode)
- Language: Python 3.10 or later
- Transport: Standard input/output (`stdio`) or Streamable HTTP (`streamable-http` on Cloud Run)
- Authentication: Application Default Credentials (OAuth 2.0 user credentials or service account) for local `stdio`, or OAuth 2.0 Web application credentials for remote HTTP
- Telemetry: Appends `google-ads-mcp/VERSION` to the `x-goog-api-client` gRPC request header for usage statistics

### How the interaction loop works

1. Request: You submit a prompt such as "How is my campaign performance this week?" or "Create a callout asset for our summer sale".
2. Discovery: The LLM inspects its available tools and resources and selects a matching `google-ads-mcp` tool.
3. Execution or dry-run validation: Read tools query the Google Ads API directly. Mutate tools first run in propose mode (`validate_only=True`) to validate inputs without committing changes (see Propose-and-confirm safety workflow).
4. Context injection: The MCP server returns structured query results, or proposed `change_items` entries and a verification `checksum` digest, to the LLM's context window.
5. Response and confirmation: The LLM presents an answer or asks you to confirm the proposed changes. After you approve, the LLM calls the mutate tool again with `validate_only=False` and the matching `checksum` value to commit the change.

## Get started

Follow these ... To deploy a shared remote service instead, see Deployment on Google Cloud.

### Prerequisites

Before you configure the server, complete the following prerequisites in your local environment and the Google Cloud console:

- Google Cloud project: Create or select a Google Cloud project with the Google Ads API enabled. Enabling the API grants Test access for testing read and mutate workflows against test accounts. To access production accounts, check the Google Ads API overview page for Explorer, Basic, or Standard access, or apply for one of these access levels. Otherwise, production calls fail with an `AuthorizationError.CLOUD_PROJECT_NOT_APPROVED_FOR_PRODUCTION` error. Google sunset developer tokens (`GOOGLE_ADS_DEVELOPER_TOKEN`) on September 9, 2026. The Google Cloud project that owns your OAuth client or service account determines your API access level.
- Credentials: Local `stdio` mode authenticates with Application Default Credentials (ADC) from an OAuth 2.0 client secret JSON file or a service account in your Cloud project. Set the `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` environment variable when needed to specify your default quota or ADC project. Remote `streamable-http` deployments instead require an OAuth 2.0 Web application Client ID and Client secret (see Deploy to Google Cloud Run).
- Local software (for `stdio` mode): Install Python 3.10 or later, `pipx`, and the `gcloud` command-line tool (used to generate user ADC files).

```
        "run",
        "--spec",
        "google-ads-mcp==0.0.6",
        "google-ads-mcp"
      ],
      "env": {
        "GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT": "PROJECT_ID",
        "GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS": "PATH_TO_CREDENTIALS_JSON"
      }
    }
  }
}

```

Replace the following:

- `PROJECT_ID`: your Google Cloud project ID.
- `PATH_TO_CREDENTIALS_JSON`: the path to the ADC JSON file printed in step 1, or to your service account key JSON file. You can omit `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` when using the default `gcloud` ADC file location.

To access client accounts through a manager account, set `GOOGLE_ADS_LOGIN_CUSTOMER_ID` (10 digits, without hyphens) in `env`, or pass the `login_customer_id` parameter on individual tool calls.

...

## Core capabilities

The following sections describe the server's read tools, partial mutate tools, and reference resources. Starting in `v0.0.6`, tools register by default with their category namespace prefix (such as `search_search`). When upgrading prompts or allowlists from unprefixed releases, update tool names or set an empty prefix (`""`) in `tools_config.yaml` (see Configure tool namespaces and read-only mode).

### Read tools

- `customers_list_accessible_customers` (tool `list_accessible_customers`): Returns the Google Ads customer IDs directly accessible to the authenticated user.
- `search_search` (tool `search`): Builds and runs GAQL`SearchStream` queries from structured parameters (`customer_id`, `resource`, and `fields`, plus optional `conditions`, `orderings`, `limit`, and `login_customer_id`) rather than a raw GAQL string. Every query appends `PARAMETERS omit_unselected_resource_names=true` to fetch resource attributes, metrics, segments, budgets, and status cleanly.
- `metadata_get_resource_metadata` (tool `get_resource_metadata`): Retrieves selectable, filterable, and sortable attributes, metrics, and segments for a Google Ads API resource type (for example, `"campaign"`). Use this metadata to discover valid query fields—including metrics and segments added in minor releases such as v26.2—before calling the `search_search` tool.

### Mutate tools (partial support)

- `assets_create_asset` (tool `create_asset`): Creates standalone Google Ads assets with dedicated parameters for `TEXT`, `IMAGE`, `YOUTUBE_VIDEO`, `SITELINK`, `CALLOUT`, and `STRUCTURED_SNIPPET` asset types. Pass the `extra_params` dictionary for other mutable `AssetService` types (such as `PRICE`, `PROMOTION`, `CALL`, or `BUSINESS_MESSAGE`), and include root-level `final_urls` alongside `sitelink_link_text` for `SITELINK` assets. Local file paths (`image_asset_path`) work in local `stdio` mode only. For remote HTTP deployments, pass the base64-encoded `image_asset_data` parameter with `image_asset_mime_type` set to `IMAGE_PNG`, `IMAGE_JPEG`, or `IMAGE_GIF` (up to 20 MB).
- `assets_upload_video_asset` (tool `upload_video_asset`): Uploads a local video file (`.3gp`, `.avi`, `.flv`, `.mkv`, `.mov`, `.mp4`, `.mpeg`, `.mpg`, `.ogg`, `.webm`, or `.wmv`) to YouTube through the Google Ads API as a FastMCP background task in local `stdio` mode only. Both `video_title` and `video_description` are required parameters. The `video_privacy` parameter accepts `UNLISTED` (default) or `PUBLIC` (allowed only on advertiser-owned brand channels with user OAuth). This tool returns a Google Ads `video_upload_id` value (and resource name), not the 11-character YouTube `video_id`. Query `you_tube_video_upload` with the `search_search` tool (filtering by `you_tube_video_upload.video_upload_id`) until `you_tube_video_upload.state = 'PROCESSED'`. Then pass `you_tube_video_upload.video_id` as the `youtube_video_id` parameter to `assets_create_asset` (`asset_type="YOUTUBE_VIDEO"`).
- `labels_manage_labels` (tool `manage_labels`): Creates, updates, and removes account labels, including name, description, and hex background color.
- `labels_manage_label_associations` (tool `manage_label_associations`): Supports `CREATE` and `REMOVE` label association operations (`UPDATE` is not supported) on `CAMPAIGN`, `CUSTOMER`, `AD_GROUP`, and `AD_GROUP_CRITERION` resources. For `CUSTOMER` resources, `resource_id` is optional and defaults to `customer_id`. Pass a composite `{ad_group_id}~{criterion_id}` ID for `AD_GROUP_CRITERION` resources, and remove associations by passing either `resource_id` and `label_id` or `association_resource_name`. Ad-level `AD_GROUP_AD` labels are not supported.

Note: Mutate support covers standalone asset creation, video uploads, and label management only. The server cannot link assets to campaigns, ad groups, or asset groups, or configure ad-level asset automation settings (such as `OVERLAY_TEXT_ON_VIDEOS` in v26.2). It also cannot create, modify, pause, or enable campaigns, ad groups, ads, budgets, or bids. For unsupported mutations, pair the server with companion code-generation tools (see Equip your agent with skills and the Developer Assistant).

### Reference resources

The server exposes four read-only MCP resources that remain mounted regardless of your `tools_config.yaml` settings:

- `resource://discovery-document`: JSON REST discovery overview of Google Ads API resources, service methods, and schemas. It complements the `metadata_get_resource_metadata` tool, which returns selectable, filterable, and sortable GAQL query fields.
- `resource://metrics`: HTML reference documentation for Google Ads API metrics.
- `resource://segments`: HTML reference documentation for Google Ads API segments.
- `resource://release-notes`: HTML Google Ads API release notes covering version changes and new features.

### Propose-and-confirm safety workflow

Every mutate tool (`assets_create_asset`, `assets_upload_video_asset`, `labels_manage_labels`, and `labels_manage_label_associations`) enforces a two-step propose-and-confirm workflow to help prevent unintended account modifications:

1. Propose (`validate_only=True`, default): Validates inputs without committing changes. The asset and label tools execute a live Google Ads API `validate_only` dry run. Because `YouTubeVideoUploadService` has no dry-run mode, `assets_upload_video_asset` instead validates the local file and binds its size and modification timestamp. Each tool returns human-readable `change_items` entries and a stateless SHA-256 `checksum` digest bound to the `customer_id` parameter and request payload.
2. Confirm (`validate_only=False`): After presenting the `change_items` list and receiving your approval, the agent calls the tool again with `validate_only=False`, the identical `customer_id` parameter and arguments, and the `checksum` value from step 1. The server rejects any missing or mismatched checksum before mutating the account.

Note: The `checksum` value is an unkeyed SHA-256 digest of the request parameters that works statelessly across Cloud Run instances. It prevents accidental parameter drift or local file swaps across turns, but does not replace access control. To hard-block mutations, disable the `labels` and `assets` namespaces in `tools_config.yaml`.

### Configure tool namespaces and read-only mode

The server bundles a default `tools_config.yaml` file with all five tool categories (`customers`, `search`, `metadata`, `labels`, and `assets`) enabled. Customize `tools_config.yaml` to selectively enable or disable individual tools or namespaces, change or remove namespace prefixes, or enforce a strictly read-only deployment.

Important: Whenever `namespaces` is non-empty, any omitted category is disabled by default, whereas an empty `namespaces: {}` mapping enables all five categories. Include every category that you want to keep enabled—a file containing only `labels: false` and `assets: false` disables the read tools too.

mcp.title: googleads/google-ads-mcp
highlights:
## Overview

The Google Ads MCP Server exposes MCP Tools and MCP Resources backed by the Google Ads API. It supports:

- **Read & reporting workflows**: GAQL queries, accessible customer discovery, resource field metadata, and API reference resources.
- **Guarded account mutations**: Asset creation, video uploads, and label management protected by a two-step **Propose & Confirm** workflow.
- **Flexible deployment**: Run locally over `stdio` with Application Default Credentials, or over **Streamable HTTP** with FastMCP's OAuth proxy and structured audit logging.

> **Notes:**
> - Connecting an LLM or agent to this server exposes your accessible Google Ads account data to that client.
> - API calls made by this server include an MCP telemetry header used by Google to collect usage statistics and improve the product.
> - Report bugs or feature requests on the GitHub issue tracker.

...

|

...

### Available Tools

By default, tools are mounted with their category namespace prefix (`<namespace>_<tool>`). Namespaces and individual tools can be customized via `tools_config.yaml` (see Configuring and Namespacing Tools).

| Default Tool Name | Namespace | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `search_search` | `search` | Read | Queries Google Ads account data using GAQL (Google Ads Query Language). |
| `metadata_get_resource_metadata` | `metadata` | Read | Retrieves selectable, filterable, and sortable field metadata for a Google Ads API resource (e.g., `campaign`). |
| `customers_list_accessible_customers` | `customers` | Read | Lists customer IDs directly accessible to the authenticated user. |
| `assets_create_asset` | `assets` | Mutate | Creates Google Ads assets (`TEXT`, `IMAGE`, `YOUTUBE_VIDEO`, `SITELINK`, `CALLOUT`, `STRUCTURED_SNIPPET`, plus additional types via `extra_params`). Note: `image_asset_path` is local `stdio` only; use base64 `image_asset_data` over HTTP. |
| `assets_upload_video_asset` | `assets` | Mutate | Uploads a local video file to YouTube via a background task so it can be referenced by video assets (local `stdio` mode only). |
| `labels_manage_labels` | `labels` | Mutate | Creates, updates, and removes account labels. |
| `labels_manage_label_associations` | `labels` | Mutate | Creates and removes label associations on `CAMPAIGN`, `CUSTOMER`, `AD_GROUP`, and `AD_GROUP_CRITERION` resources. |

...

### Propose & Confirm Safety Workflow

All mutate tools (`assets_create_asset`, `assets_upload_video_asset`, `labels_manage_labels`, and `labels_manage_label_associations`) enforce a mandatory two-step safety workflow:

1. **Propose (`validate_only=True`, default)**: Validates the operation (including a Google Ads API `validate_only` dry run where supported) without committing changes. Returns human-readable `change_items` and a cryptographic `checksum` bound to the `customer_id` and parameters.
2. **Confirm (`validate_only=False`)**: After explicit user approval, pass the exact same parameters and `customer_id` along with the `checksum` from step 1. Missing or mismatched checksums are rejected before mutating the account.

mcp.title: Open Source Google Ads API MCP Server  |  Google for Developers
highlights:
Tuesday, October 7, 2025

 We're thrilled to announce the open source release of the Google Ads API Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server, available here. This project marks a significant step in democratizing access to Google Ads data for the next generation of AI tools and agent developers. 

 The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is the open standard that allows Large Language Models (LLMs), like Google Gemini, to connect with and act upon external data sources and applications. By releasing an MCP Server specifically for the Google Ads API, we are making it possible for any MCP-compatible AI application to understand and analyze advertising campaigns through natural language. 

 This initial release is read-only, meaning it can be used for reporting and diagnostics but will not make changes to your account. 

 Please use the GitHub repo for technical issues with the MCP server.

mcp.title: Google Ads MCP server gains 4 write tools, still can't change budgets
highlights:
Google released version 0.0.6 of its open-source Google Ads MCP server on November 2, 2026, and with it the first tools in the project's public history that can change a Google Ads account. The release adds four write tools that create assets, upload videos to YouTube and manage labels, each gated behind a two-step dry run and checksum. Those tools are switched on by default. No announcement accompanied the release, and Google's developer integration guide, last updated on October 30, still describes the server as strictly read-only.

...

...

The checksum therefore proves the parameters did not change. It does not prove that a dry run took place, or that anyone approved one. The message returned after validation tells the AI model to show the proposed changes to the user and wait for explicit confirmation, but that is an instruction to the model, not a control the server enforces.

...

Google's guide, titled "Google Ads MCP server: Developer integration guide" and last updated on October 30, 2026, lists the server's key specifications as "Mode: Read-only (current release)." Its section on core capabilities describes only the three read tools and ends with a note: "This implementation is strictly read-only. It cannot modify bids, pause campaigns, or create new assets."

For anyone running version 0.0.6, the first and last of those claims no longer hold: the server is not read-only, and it can create assets. Bids and campaign status remain out of reach.
